compareCandidate.label: Data point vs. statistic
compareCandidate.description: A data point is one raw observation; a statistic like the mean is a summary computed from many points.

plainLanguageExplanation: A data point is one single piece of information — one child's height, one day's temperature, one quiz score. It is the smallest unit of data. Collect many data points and you have a dataset. Each point has a value (like 150 cm) and usually a label (like 'Ali'). Charts show data points grouped or graphed, and statistics like the mean, median, and mode are all computed from the individual points. Understanding data starts with understanding that every graph is built from individual points.

whyItMatters: Every chart, graph, and statistic is built from data points. Recognizing a single point — and where it lives in a dataset — is the first and most basic skill in statistics.
didYouKnow: The tallest data point in the dataset, the shortest, and every point in between — even the weird one that looks like a mistake — all count as data points and all influence your summary.
compareReason: Students confuse the raw observation with its summary — comparing one point with the average computed from all of them makes the difference visible.
